speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Temperature 98.7°F (37.1°C), Blood Pressure 122/81 mmHg, Heart Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate 15 breaths/min, Oxygen Saturation 99% on room air. Neurological Exam: Nystagmus noted with bilateral decreased hearing; unstable tandem gait with reported imbalance. Positional Testing (Dix-Hallpike/Head Rotation): Laying patient flat rapidly with head turned to each side did not provoke symptoms. Basic Audiometry: Bilateral decreased hearing sensitivity. Laboratory Tests (CBC, Electrolytes): Within normal limits. Imaging (Head CT/MRI): No acute abnormalities, no signs of stroke or significant lesions.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of bilateral hearing loss and persistent vertigo following a recent viral illness strongly suggests labyrinthitis rather than BPPV, given the negative Dix-Hallpike. I have sufficient clinical and test data to form a conclusion.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Bilateral Viral Labyrinthitis
